lines: Taylor Nguyen
+1 (555) 010-6642 | taylor.nguyen@example.com | example.com/code/tnguyen
EDUCATION
Westfield State University | M.S. in Computer Science | Metro City, USA | Sep 2024 - Expected Jun 2026
Westfield State University | B.S. in Computer Science | Metro City, USA | Sep 2019 - Jun 2023
EXPERIENCE
Lumen Travel | Frontend Engineering Intern | Metro City, USA | Jun 2025 - Sep 2025
- Rebuilt the hotel search results page in React with server-side rendering, cutting median load time from 3.8s to 1.6s and raising bookings per search 9% in an A/B test.
- Cut the booking flow's JavaScript from 410 KB to 260 KB by code-splitting the calendar and map widgets.
- Added keyboard navigation and screen-reader labels to the date picker, fixing all 14 accessibility issues flagged in the audit.
- Moving image resizing to the CDN, inlining critical CSS, preloading the two web fonts and deferring the analytics script, raised the checkout page's Lighthouse performance score from 52 to 91.
- Cut the landing page's largest contentful paint from 4.1s to 1.2s by adding loading="lazy" to the hero image.
- Documented the design-system tokens in Storybook so designers could check spacing and color values without asking engineers.
Westfield State University | Web Developer, IT Services | Metro City, USA | Apr 2024 - Aug 2024
- Cut the university sites' JavaScript bundle by 60% by converting their PNG images to WebP.
- Interviewed 8 department editors about publishing; the findings led to a preview mode that cut broken pages reported by students from 30 to 6 a month.
- Writes the accessibility checklist for all university web pages, reducing failed audits from 12 to 2 a semester.
- Rebuilt the course-catalog search with client-side filtering, cutting search time from 4 seconds to under 1.
PROJECTS
Transit Arrival Web App | Independent Project | TypeScript, React | Oct 2025 - Present
- Built a progressive web app showing live bus arrivals for 400 stops, used by about 900 riders a week.
- Cut cold-start time on slow 3G from 3.0s to 1.5s, a 75% improvement, by caching the stop list offline.
- Raised weekly returning riders by 10% in the first month, from 30% to 40%, by adding saved stops.
Library Room Booking | Hackathon, Team of 4 | Vue | Feb 2024 - Mar 2024
- Worked on the frontend of the booking flow using React and TypeScript.
- Wrote the booking calendar component and its tests, handling overlapping bookings and time-zone changes.
- Presented the demo to the library staff and handed over the code with setup notes.
SKILLS
Tools: TypeScript, React, Vue, Storybok, Angular
Methods: server-side rendering, accessibility, component testing

items.says: Make the code URL lead directly to a public profile or portfolio.
Replace the phone number and address if they are placeholders.
items.because: Contact details should be the ones you intend to use when applying.

items.says: Confirm the expected M.S. graduation date when you submit the résumé.
Specify what “load time” measures.
items.because: It could be confused with another performance metric.

items.says: Make sure the A/B test supports attributing the booking increase to this change.
Clarify whether the JavaScript sizes are transferred, compressed, or uncompressed.
items.because: The comparison should be unambiguous.

items.says: Scope “all 14” to the issues identified in that audit.
items.because: It could imply the date picker has no remaining accessibility issues.

items.says: Change the opening construction to read as a completed action.
items.because: It should be consistent with the other bullets.

items.says: Identify which of the four changes you made yourself.
items.because: Listing four changes makes your contribution harder to distinguish.

items.says: The stated cause of the LCP improvement appears inconsistent.
items.because: Lazy-loading an above-the-fold hero image generally delays the LCP image.

items.says: Add evidence of adoption or time saved if available.
items.because: The current benefit is less concrete than the other bullets.

items.says: Converting PNGs to WebP would not ordinarily reduce a JavaScript bundle by 60%.
items.because: It can reduce image bytes or page weight instead.

items.says: Make sure the broken-page counts cover comparable periods.
Support the connection between preview mode and the drop in broken pages.
“Writes” is in the wrong tense.
items.because: The role ended in August 2024.

items.says: Clarify whether you authored the checklist, maintained it, or both.
Define what the four-to-under-one-second figure measures.
items.because: Client-side filtering does not necessarily make initial page loading faster.

items.says: Be ready to explain how you measure approximately 900 weekly riders.
The 75% improvement figure is incorrect.
items.because: Going from 3.0s to 1.5s is a 50% reduction in time.

items.says: Check whether offline caching affects the measured “cold-start” condition.
items.because: Those terms may conflict.

items.says: Calling the change from 30% to 40% a 10% increase confuses percentage points with relative increase.
items.because: It is a 10-percentage-point increase.

items.says: The heading’s Vue framework contradicts the frontend bullet’s React and TypeScript.
items.because: The technologies listed in both places should align.

items.says: The frontend bullet’s React and TypeScript contradict the heading’s Vue framework.
items.because: The technologies listed in both places should align.

items.says: Confirm that the component or its tests covered overlap and time-zone cases.
items.because: The bullet implies they did.

items.says: Consider cutting the demo-and-handoff bullet if space is needed.
items.because: It says less about the software or its outcome than the calendar bullet.

items.says: “Storybok” is misspelled.
items.because: It should be “Storybook.”

items.says: Include Angular only if you can discuss work you have done with it.
Consider separating languages, frameworks, and tools.
